evidence: AI plugin/registration.rs:286-313 exports BehaviorNodeRegistryService and registers the owner-revocation callback against the same manager Arc; plugin_sdk/src/registration.rs:151-157 writes it into the source registry. RuntimePluginRegistrationReport::from_plugin (registration_report/plugin.rs:16-61) stores that registry. Catalog extension_report/runtime.rs:11 creates a default target and extension_merge/runtime.rs:71-85 reaches contributions/extension.rs:41-147; the merge copies interface exports (same provider Arc) and remaps owner IDs but carries no listener, and descriptor/render helper families do not carry one. extension_registry/runtime_extension_registry.rs:76,84-91 keeps listeners private; :219-230 only notifies listeners of the registry being revoked. Therefore revocation on the merged registry cannot invoke the AI callback. manager/behavior_tree.rs:142-187 shows callback cleanup removes nodes, retires dependent trees and active instances. Current repository invocations of revoke_owner_registrations are test-only; this is a confirmed conditional API/merge contract defect, not evidence of a currently occurring production unload failure. AI tests/registration.rs:267-363 revoke a direct registry/report without catalog merge; the merged interface test at contributions/extension.rs:241-310 does not register any listener. Detailed review: EVIDENCE.md and current caller hashes in source_manifest.json.
impact_or_question: When an owner contribution was added through the catalog's merged BehaviorNodeRegistry service, revoking that owner on the final merged RuntimeExtensionRegistry removes registry-owned contributions but never notifies the AI manager callback. Externally owned behavior-node descriptors and dependent compiled trees/instances remain in the shared manager. No production caller of this revocation API is currently visible; the defect is triggered by invoking the supported API after merge. Listener owner IDs and callback arguments must obey a deliberate source-to-final owner mapping; simply copying source numeric IDs would not establish that contract.
next_action: Add catalog-level and project-target-filtered regressions that register an owner-scoped listener, merge the source report, add an externally owned AI node through the final bridge, then revoke on the final registry and assert callback delivery plus dependent tree retirement. Include differing source/final owner IDs and an unselected listener-owning module. Design a registry projection API that preserves selected listeners and consistently rebases listener ownership, callback revoked-owner arguments, and service-held owner state; repair behavior in a separately authorized task.
